newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel market quietly watches tumbling crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel market quietly watches tumbling crude.

text.p: NWE fuel oil was softer on Monday. Players were kept quiet wary of getting caught by falling crude.
"Nothing much has happened. Crude needs to stabilise before people feel confident to trade again," commented one trader.
High sulphur cracked barges had up to $3 shaved off with $116.50 fob ARA heard traded.
Cargoes were also weaker, but not to the same degree.
Traders said supplies were fair, but that no one would buy today given crude's drop.
"End-users will be looking for it to bottom out before picking up product," said a dealer.

Between 70-80,000 tonnes of very poor quality 3.5 percent sulphur was sold out of the U.S at $109 cif Rotterdam. Some traders thought the material, part of the surplus fuel that has become available after a shut-down at a coking unit in the U.S Gulf, might be headed into Romania.

The low sulphur market was pegged softer but quiet. December paper was heard offered as low as $132.50 fob NWE and wet barrels were put a couple of dollars higher. Dealers were mixed between those who thought the very weak fuel prices in the U.S Gulf would prompt transatlantic trade and others who said strong natural gas prices would keep the American fuel at home.
